redFirst.basis: `python3 plugins/audit/tests/test_drive_phase.py --selftest --stage ci-block` in a throwaway tree at HEAD exited 1 on "AttributeError: module 'ci_cadence_mod' has no attribute 'ci_run'" (read as python), and the task introduces 'ci_run': absent from HEAD's plugins/audit/scripts/governance/drive-phase.py, plugins/audit/scripts/config/_config_rules.py, plugins/audit/reference/config.md, plugins/audit/schema/audit-config.schema.json, plugins/audit/scripts/panel/_panel_settings.py, plugins/audit/scripts/status/_doctor_setup.py and present in the working tree's plugins/audit/scripts/governance/drive-phase.py; a second run with the working tree's implementation copied in exited 0 without that error, its tests reaching their assertions; run without CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR; dependencies linked from the project root, entry by entry as symlinks: node_modules - .cache, .vite, .vite-temp are not linked and a new entry a runner makes beside the links stays in the throwaway, but a write into a linked entry lands in the project's own node_modules and is not watched; no .npmrc to carry or drop

outcome.technical: drive-phase.py: new section 'CI at a cadence' (ci_run seam, ci_due, ci_settle, ci_dispatch, ci_after_close, ci_before_signoff); close_task calls ci_after_close after the done verb, sign_off calls ci_before_signoff. At a due close it pushes +<sha>:refs/heads/ci/<phase lower> and runs `gh workflow run <workflow> --ref ci/<phase>` without waiting; the next close (and sign-off) does one `gh run list` read for that sha; failure/timed_out/startup_failure files a high bug via audit-task.py bug-add naming branch, sha, run id and URL; a run still going/not listed/unreadable is said and nothing is piled on; a failed push/dispatch is said and retried at the next close; no ci.cadence = zero CI calls. _config_rules.py: root key ci (KNOWN_CI, KNOWN_CI_CADENCE), ci_cadence_setting() refusing closes<1, hours<=0, empty cadence, blank workflow; _check_ci in validate_config; OFF_ROOT['hooks DEFAULTS']['ci'] with reason. schema/audit-config.schema.json publishes ci (cadence.closes, cadence.hours, workflow). _panel_settings.py: a 'ci' Settings group with leaf controls ci.cadence.closes, ci.cadence.hours, ci.workflow and FIELD_HELP; test__panel_settings.py: container map + group tuple + case ps4. _doctor_setup.py: check_ci_cadence row 'ci cadence' reached from check_config, reading the config FILE (not the hooks merge), reporting effective triggers, workflow and source path OK, the absence said as landing-only (naming 'no config file' when there is none), the driver's own refusal as a finding, and nothing for an unreadable config; test__doctor_setup.py cases ci1-ci7. New reference/config.md. plugins/audit/README.md carries the ci.cadence and ci.workflow rows: README is NOT in the task's files and the brief names no follower rule for it; it is kept because test__config_rules cv1 reads the README's Configuration table as one of the surfaces that must publish every KNOWN_ROOT key, and it reported 'README: does not publish ci' before the rows were added - reverting it turns cv1 red, and the rows cannot move to reference/config.md because cv1 does not read that file. The plan gate allowed the edit (docs path). test_drive_phase.py: stage ci-block, 12 cases titled with the tests.add clause, ci_run faked so no remote or gh is touched. Evidence: ci-block 12/12; full `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py --quiet` exit 0 (335/335 files ok, 16552 cases); ruff and vermin clean. PREMISE CORRECTIONS: (1) the drive did NOT already push ci/ branches - only tools/release.py does, for release tags - so there was no existing landing dispatch and 'absent, it dispatches only at landing' is asserted as zero CI calls at any close; no landing dispatch was added. (2) 'ci-red-files-bug' does not exist (P128.1-0h5, which would have read failing jobs and cases, is cancelled), so a red files a plain high bug naming the run and URL without per-job/case detail.
outcome.descriptive: A phase can ask CI about itself every N closes or H hours, non-blocking, with a red filed as a bug; schema, Settings panel group and doctor row publish and report it.

testsAdded: plugins/audit/tests/test_drive_phase.py: with ci.cadence every 3 closes the drive dispatches CI on the third close and not before, never waits on it, and reads its verdict at the next close; absent, it dispatches only at landing
claims: claims: (1) 'no ci.cadence = no CI call' is held by the absent case asserting calls == [] across a full drive with the seam faked; (2) 'never waits' is held by no watch/--exit-status argv, the fourth task closing while the run is out, and an in_progress run still finishing the drive - NOT held for real gh latency, the seam is faked; (3) the real ci_run subprocess path (stdin DEVNULL, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0) was never run against a real remote or gh; (4) the doctor reads the config file, so a setting only the hooks' merged config carries would not show - ci is deliberately not in DEFAULTS.
